metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Most follow-up questions name specific identifiers or decisions in the generated code, such as 'Any reason for the store_git function over pass(s) git?', 'What is ensure_line?', 'What supplies the vault_dir variable?', 'Summarise the responsibility split between vault_pass and vault_history' and 'Is it right to hardcode vault here?', and none of these could be asked without reading the output.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: GIT_PRACTICE.md was in context and most commit subjects follow the conventional form, but compliance is partial: 'text: fix syntax based on linter' uses a type the rule does not allow, and the 'vault' scope is used in a repository that is not a monorepo, which the rule forbids.

metrics.name: output_amendments
metrics.title: Output amendments
metrics.evidence: 244 of 853 generated lines were rewritten after the author challenged them

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: The median is 53 generated lines across 14 producing prompts, inside the 50 to 200 band; most prompts name specific units of work (for example dropping merge support, inlining vault_dir_exists, adding a --help flag), but some brief prompts produced more than 200 lines each, such as 'Ok, implement this' (233 lines), 'Both' (212) and the CHANGELOG request (215).

metrics.name: generative_comments
metrics.title: Generative comments
metrics.evidence: 4 comment lines over 753 lines of code, against a repository baseline of 0.007
